Let
\[
Z=Z(G)=\{(0,0,t):t\in\mathbb F_p\}.
\]
For any subgroup \(X\ge Z\) of order \(p^3\), its image \(W=X/Z\) is a \(2\)-dimensional subspace of
\[
\mathbb F_p^2\oplus \mathbb F_p^2.
\]
The commutator is
\[
[(u,v,t),(u',v',t')]=(0,0,u\cdot v'-u'\cdot v),
\]
so \(X\) is abelian exactly when \(W\) is totally isotropic for
\[
\omega((u,v),(u',v'))=u\cdot v'-u'\cdot v.
\]

The two coordinate-intersection conditions say \(W\) meets neither coordinate plane nontrivially. Hence
\[
W=\{(u,Mu):u\in\mathbb F_p^2\}
\]
for an invertible \(2\times2\) matrix \(M\). The isotropic condition gives
\[
u^T Mu'=u'^T Mu \quad\forall u,u',
\]
so \(M\) is symmetric. The diagonal condition says
\[
\dim\ker(M-I)=1.
\]
Thus admissible subgroups correspond exactly to matrices
\[
M=I+H,
\]
where \(H\) is a nonzero rank-one symmetric \(2\times2\) matrix and
\[
\operatorname{tr}H\ne -1.
\]

Now classify such \(H\) by its kernel line \(L\subset \mathbb F_p^2\). For each projective line \(L\), the rank-one symmetric matrices with kernel \(L\) form one nonzero scalar family. If \(L\) is isotropic for \(x^2+y^2\), then every nonzero scalar is allowed, giving \(p-1\) choices. Otherwise exactly one scalar has trace \(-1\), giving \(p-2\) choices.

The number of isotropic lines is
\[
r=\begin{cases}
2,&p\equiv1\pmod4,\\
0,&p\equiv3\pmod4.
\end{cases}
\]
For two admissible matrices \(M=I+H\), \(N=I+K\),
\[
A\cap B=Z
\]
is equivalent to \(H-K\) being invertible. Since \(H,K\) are rank-one symmetric matrices, this happens exactly when their kernel lines are distinct.

Therefore the required number is
\[
\left(\sum_L n_L\right)^2-\sum_L n_L^2,
\]
where \(n_L=p-1\) for isotropic \(L\), and \(n_L=p-2\) otherwise.

Hence
\[
\boxed{
\begin{cases}
p(p+1)(p-2)^2,&p\equiv3\pmod4,\\[2mm]
p^4-3p^3+4p^2-4p+2,&p\equiv1\pmod4.
\end{cases}}
\]
